chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, the people of religion have signs by which they are known: truthfulness of speech, fulfilling the trust, loyalty to the covenant, maintaining kinship ties, mercy towards the weak, little intimacy with women, giving of good, good character, breadth of disposition, and following knowledge and what brings one closer to God, the Mighty and Majestic. Blessed are they and good is their return!

And Tuba is a tree in Paradise, its root is in the abode of the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), and there is no believer except that in his abode is a branch of it. No desire for anything occurs to his heart except that branch brings it to him. Even if a rider hastening traveled in its shade for a hundred years, he would not exit from it, and if a crow flew from its bottom, it would not reach its top until it fell from old age. Indeed, in this, desire! The believer is occupied with himself, while the people are at ease from him. And when the night covers him, he spreads his face and prostrates to God, the Mighty and Majestic, with the noble parts of his body, supplicating the One who created him for the liberation of his neck. Indeed, be like this!

key_terms.أهل الدين: Ahl al-Din - People of religion, those who truly practice faith
key_terms.طوبى: Tuba - A tree in Paradise; the word also means blessedness and happiness
key_terms.فكاك رقبته: Fakak raqabatihi - Liberation of his neck, i.e., salvation from the Fire

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the people of religion according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali describes the distinguishing signs of the people of faith -- truthfulness, trustworthiness, mercy, good character -- and then depicts the wondrous tree Tuba in Paradise, which has a branch in every believer's home fulfilling every desire. He concludes with a portrait of the devout believer who, when night falls, prostrates before God seeking salvation, and exhorts the audience to embody these qualities. This sermon, transmitted through the golden chain from Imam al-Sadiq, integrates Quranic imagery (13:29) with ethical and eschatological themes.
